title: IdeaForge’s revenue jumps over 5X to Rs 69 Cr in Q1 FY27; loss narrows 89%
summary:
Drone maker IdeaForge Technologies saw revenue balloon more than fivefold in Q1 FY27, while losses narrowed sharply. However, it slipped back into the red after a profitable March quarter, with revenue also falling sequentially.

IdeaForge’s revenue from operations jumped to Rs 68.58 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 12.78 crore in Q1 FY26, registering a 436.6% YoY growth, according to financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The company reported Rs 1.96 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 70.5 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 16.7 crore in Q1 FY26.
 
Cost of materials remained the company’s largest expense, jumping 7.15X to Rs 34.97 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 4.89 crore in the year-ago quarter. Employee benefit expenses increased 20.9% to Rs 15.1 crore from Rs 12.49 crore, while depreciation rose 44.9% to Rs 14.2 crore from Rs 9.8 crore.
 
Meanwhile, finance costs jumped 5.49X to Rs 2.03 crore from Rs 0.37 crore, while other expenses increased 11.9% to Rs 16.2 crore from Rs 14.48 crore. Overall, IdeaForge’s total expenses rose 96.4% to Rs 82.5 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 42 crore in Q1 FY26.
 
As a result, IdeaForge’s loss narrowed 89% to Rs 2.59 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 23.56 crore in Q1 FY26.
 
On a sequential basis, the company’s operating revenue declined around 51% from Rs 141 crore in Q4 FY26. IdeaForge had reported a net profit of Rs 60 crore in Q4 FY26, before slipping back into the red in the June quarter.
 
In June 2026, ideaForge Technology had raised Rs 500 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) by allotting 62.89 lakh shares at Rs 795 per share.
 
IdeaForge’s shares were closed at Rs 902.10 apiece on Friday, taking the company’s market capitalisation to Rs 4,483 crore.

title: Zostel withdraws latest plea before Delhi HC in OYO dispute
summary:
Zostel has withdrawn its latest application before the Delhi High Court in its long-running dispute with PRISM, the parent company of OYO.
The application was taken up by the Delhi High Court on Monday, August 10. The court allowed Zostel to withdraw the plea with liberty to approach it again. It also declined to intervene in Zostel’s complaint before the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
The matter was briefly heard last week, when an issue concerning Zostel’s legal representation came up. Its previous counsel informed the court that legal fees remained unpaid, while Zostel had engaged new counsel for the latest application. The court then adjourned the matter to August 10. When the case came up again, Zostel withdrew the application.
The latest development comes a month after Zostel withdrew an earlier application before the Delhi High Court on July 8.
The dispute dates back to OYO’s proposed acquisition of Zostel in 2015. Zostel claims it is entitled to nearly 7% stake in OYO, with the share entitlement remaining unresolved.
In May 2025, the Delhi High Court set aside the arbitral award underlying Zostel’s claims, holding that there was no concluded deal between the parties. Zostel’s Section 37 appeal against the judgment remains pending before the Delhi High Court.
Separately, Zostel recently approached SEBI over OYO’s draft IPO disclosures, alleging that the filing omitted material details related to the dispute. Zostel sought a review of the disclosures as OYO prepares for its IPO process.
A PRISM spokesperson said the latest order came barely a month after Zostel withdrew its previous application. The spokesperson maintained that Zostel’s applications were frivolous and not maintainable.

title: Info Edge’s Shiksha faces AI traffic headwinds as Q1 billings fall 23%
summary:
Info Edge’s education business Shiksha faced traffic and demand-related headwinds in Q1 FY27, with the company attributing the slowdown partly to changes in Google search driven by the rise of AI.
According to the company's Q1 FY27 earning presentation, Shiksha’s billings declined 22.8% year-on-year to Rs 35 crore in the quarter, while revenue fell 11.9% to Rs 44 crore. Operating PBT declined 48.8% year-on-year to Rs 3 crore. Cash from operations stood at a negative Rs 7 crore.
The traffic pressure comes as AI-generated search experiences increasingly affect referral traffic from Google, a key acquisition channel for content-led platforms such as Shiksha. 
To counter the traffic pressure, Shiksha is investing in comprehensive, student-friendly content and strengthening its domestic counselling business. The company also plans to continue investing in its Study Abroad platform. 
The overseas education market is facing another shift. Info Edge said student interest in studying in the US remains subdued, while preferences are moving towards the UK, Australia and European markets. This shift could require Shiksha to adapt its offerings and counselling services across different study destinations. 
Despite the near-term challenges, Shiksha continues to operate at significant scale. The platform lists more than 68,000 colleges and 574,000 courses and covers over 1,150 entrance exams. Between July 2025 and June 2026, it recorded more than 6.3 million annual registrations, 467 million page views and 228 million visits. 
In Q1 FY27, Info Edge reported consolidated revenue from operations of Rs 881 crore, with Shiksha contributing around 5% of the total operating revenue. Meanwhile, the company’s overall profit rose 43% year-on-year to Rs 490 crore during the quarter.

title: Ather's demand outpaces capacity as monthly pre-orders cross 50,000
summary:
Ather Energy's latest earnings call showed a sharp mismatch between demand and supply, with the electric scooter maker's monthly pre-orders crossing 50,000 while its existing capacity remains well below that level. The company is now accelerating capacity expansion, preparing for a new lower-priced scooter and raising fresh capital to support the next phase of growth.
Ather said it was receiving more than 50,000 pre-orders a month, compared with around 30,000 units retailed monthly in the first quarter. Based on this demand, management estimates it could have sold another 13,000-15,000 units per month if supply was available.
The supply constraint is also visible at the retail level. Dealer inventory has fallen from around 14 days to just three days, while existing stores are currently fulfilling only 50-60% of demand. Some dealers have stopped taking fresh bookings as waiting periods have stretched to two months or more.
Ather currently has annual production capacity of around 4.2 lakh units, with its Hosur facility capable of producing about 35,000 scooters a month. The company expects the first phase of its AURIC facility to take total annual capacity to 9.2 lakh units later this calendar year.
The company is also evaluating the second phase of AURIC, which could add another 5 lakh units of annual capacity and take the total to 14.2 lakh units. However, Ather has not started investments in Phase 2 and expects to provide more clarity over the next one or two quarters.
To fund this expansion, Ather recently completed a Rs 1,300 crore QIP and is seeking shareholder approval for another Rs 1,200 crore preference issue. The planned Rs 2,500 crore fundraise will be used to accelerate capacity at Ather and its suppliers, support new product launches and strengthen the balance sheet amid commodity and supply pressures.
The upcoming lower-priced EL scooter will be another key capacity driver. Ather plans to build capacity for around 60,000 EL units per month across Hosur and AURIC. The company expects the scooter to initially have a stronger focus on northern and middle India, where management sees demand for more affordable variants.
Interestingly, Ather expects at least 75% of EL buyers to opt for AtherStack Pro, despite the scooter's lower price point. Management also expects EL to compete more directly with Rizta than with the 450, although it could eventually build Rizta on the EL platform if demand warrants it.
Beyond scooters, Ather is building a second revenue stream. Non-vehicle revenue now accounts for 14% of operating revenue, with AtherStack Pro the largest contributor. Management said service revenue could offer a larger opportunity over time, noting that established two-wheeler companies generate around 10-12% of revenue from services, compared with Ather's current 2-3%.
With demand running ahead of production, the immediate challenge for Ather is no longer just generating demand but converting existing demand into deliveries. The company's next phase will depend on how quickly it can add capacity, ramp up EL and improve its non-vehicle revenue mix.

According to its filing with the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Info Edge’s consolidated revenue rose to Rs 881 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 791 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.

Its recruitment solutions business, led by Naukri, remained the largest revenue contributor, with revenue rising 12% year-on-year to Rs 629 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 562 crore in Q1 FY26.
Meanwhile, real estate platform 99acres reported revenue of Rs 130 crore in Q1 FY27, up from Rs 111 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.
The company’s matchmaking segment, which includes Jeevansathi and Aisle, contributed Rs 38 crore and Rs 12 crore, respectively, during the quarter. Meanwhile, Shiksha’s revenue declined 12% year-on-year to Rs 44 crore.
The company added Rs 192 crore non operating income, which pushed its overall income to Rs 1,073 crore in Q1 FY27.
On the expense side, employee benefit expenses remained the company’s largest cost component at Rs 341 crore in Q1 FY27, followed by advertisement expenses of Rs 119 crore. Overall expenses remained largely flat at Rs 580 crore during the quarter.
Led by steady year-on-year growth in operating revenue, controlled costs, and healthy non-operating income, the company’s profit rose 43% year-on-year to Rs 490 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 343 crore in Q1 FY26.
On a quarterly basis, the company’s profit declined 35% from Rs 756 crore in Q4 FY26, which was boosted by higher other income.
As of 3:05 PM today, shares of Info Edge were trading at around Rs 1,272.5 taking the company’s market capitalization to around Rs 82,518 crore or $8.7 billion.

title: GalaxEye acquires spacecraft engineering company StarOps
summary:
Space technology startup GalaxEye has acquired Bengaluru-based spacecraft engineering company StarOps.
The acquisition brings StarOps’ proprietary technologies, qualified satellite platforms and systems engineering expertise to GalaxEye, along with an experienced engineering team. Several members of the team previously worked at TeamIndus on its Lunar Lander and Rover projects. Their experience across mission design, spacecraft development and end-of-life operations will add to GalaxEye’s capabilities across the satellite value chain.
Founded in 2022, StarOps develops satellite platforms and works on the indigenisation of spacecraft technologies in India. The acquisition adds its experience in satellite design, development and qualification to GalaxEye’s internal capabilities.
StarOps has expertise across spacecraft systems engineering, mission operations, propulsion, avionics, flight computing, guidance and navigation, structures and mechanisms, electrical systems, programme management and ground operations. The company has achieved more than 66% indigenisation across its satellite systems and has developed technologies aimed at reducing dependence on global supply chains.
The acquisition also adds StarOps’ portfolio of spacecraft technologies and engineering capabilities to GalaxEye. This includes qualified satellite bus platforms across the 50 kg, 150 kg and 250 kg classes, proprietary subsystem technologies, qualification heritage, testing infrastructure and engineering tools.
The deal will expand GalaxEye’s in-house engineering capabilities and add spacecraft technologies across multiple stages of the satellite development process. The companies said the integration will support product development, vertical integration and the delivery of end-to-end space missions from concept and development to operations.
Co-founded in 2021 by Suyash Singh, Denil Chawda, Kishan Thakkar, Pranit Mehta, Rakshit Bhatt and Satya Chakravarthy, GalaxEye is developing Earth observation capabilities through its proprietary OptoSAR technology. The technology combines Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and optical imaging to provide day-and-night and all-weather imaging capabilities.
The acquisition comes amid increased M&A activity in India’s startup ecosystem, with recent transactions spanning fintech, consumer, SaaS, proptech and deep-tech companies. Recent deals include Aurum PropTech’s acquisition of Housing.com for an enterprise value of Rs 458 crore, Meesho’s Rs 202 crore acquisition of Kirana Club, and MoEngage’s acquisition of AI startup Aampe.

title: Aum Ventures announces first close of Rs 750 Cr India Innovation Fund II
summary:
Early-stage venture capital firm Aum Ventures has announced the first close of its India Innovation Fund II at Rs 225 crore.
The fund has a target corpus of Rs 750 crore (approximately $80 million) and will invest in early-stage startups building IP-led technology companies from India for global markets.
According to the Mumbai-based VC firm, the first close attracted participation from both existing and new investors, with more than 65% of commitments coming from international limited partners across the US, the Middle East and other global markets. The investors include family offices, entrepreneurs and strategic investors.
Aum Ventures said it will support portfolio companies with access to global markets, strategic partnerships, talent and industry expertise across India, the US, Israel and the Middle East.
The new fund will focus on sectors such as space tech, AI, semiconductors, aerospace, defence tech, robotics, energy transition, advanced manufacturing and other IP-led technologies. It will primarily invest at the pre-seed and seed stages, with initial investments typically ranging from $750,000 to $2 million. The fund will also reserve capital for follow-on investments through Series A and Series B rounds. Over its lifecycle, the fund is expected to invest in 25–30 companies.
Aum Ventures was an early institutional investor in Skyroot Aerospace, which became India's first space tech unicorn and recently completed the launch of its Vikram-1 rocket.
Fund II builds on Aum Ventures' first fund, launched in 2023. The firm said the fund has recorded a gross MOIC of 2.23x and a gross IRR of 53% so far. It has also exited Sharang Shakti, which was acquired by LAT Aerospace.
Aum Ventures' portfolio includes Skyroot Aerospace, Azimuth AI, Cosmoserve Space, Sanyark Space, Sully.ai and Latentai, among others, across frontier technology sectors.
Several Indian venture capital firms have recently launched dedicated funds focused on deep tech, reflecting increased investor activity in areas such as AI, defence tech, space tech, semiconductors, robotics and climate technology. Shastra VC launched a $100 million deep tech and AI fund in May 2026, while IIT Madras Research Park and Unicorn India Ventures announced the Rs 600 crore IIT Madras Unicorn Frontier Fund I, with a Rs 400 crore greenshoe option, to invest in 25–30 frontier tech startups.
Piper Serica recently raised Rs 300 crore in the first close of its Rs 800 crore Bharat Tech Fund, which targets deep tech companies in AI, robotics, advanced materials and space technology. Kalaari Capital and Blue Ashva Capital have also been exploring dedicated deep tech funds of around Rs 500–600 crore and Rs 300–400 crore, respectively, as investors look to increase exposure to India's R&D and innovation ecosystem.

title: Bernstein raises Paytm target to Rs 2,200 on UPI MDR upside
summary:
Bernstein, a global investment research and brokerage firm, has retained its ‘Outperform’ rating on Paytm parent One97 Communications and raised its target price to Rs 2,200 from Rs 1,500 on the potential introduction of Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions.
The brokerage has moved UPI MDR from an “optionality” to its base case from FY28 in its estimates. It assumes around 35 bps MDR on a subset of UPI person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions.
Bernstein expects Paytm to capture around 3-4 bps of incremental net payment margin from UPI MDR. The brokerage estimates that MDR could add Rs 1,320 crore, Rs 1,690 crore and Rs 2,160 crore to EBITDA in FY28E, FY29E and FY30E, respectively.
It has also raised its FY30E EPS (estimated earnings per share) by around 30% to Rs 106. Bernstein expects Paytm’s GMV to increase from Rs 30.9 lakh Cr in FY27E to Rs 56.6 lakh Cr by FY30E.
According to the brokerage, the key risk has now shifted from whether MDR will be introduced to how much of the published rate Paytm can retain amid competition in merchant acquiring and pressure on take rates.
The development comes after the government clarified that consumers will not be charged for UPI transactions. Any MDR, if introduced, will apply only to select merchant transactions above a certain threshold. The government also said a sustainable revenue model is needed to support investments in UPI infrastructure, cybersecurity and fraud prevention.
Paytm remained the third-largest UPI player in June 2026, with 1.80 billion transactions, according to NPCI data. The fintech major accounted for 7.92% of UPI transaction volume and 6.66% of transaction value, processing transactions worth Rs 1.93 lakh crore during the month.
Paytm made its stock market debut in July 2021 at an issue price of Rs 2,150, a level the stock has not revisited since its listing. Shares of Paytm are currently trading at Rs 1,558. The stock has gained around 20% so far in 2026.

title: Delhivery posts Rs 2,931 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit declines 65%
summary:
Logistics company Delhivery reported a 27.8% year-on-year increase in revenue in Q1 FY27, while its profit declined sharply during the quarter.


Delhivery’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 2,931 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,294 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The company primarily earns revenue from its logistics services, including warehousing, last-mile delivery, and the design and deployment of logistics management systems. Other income declined 12.3% to Rs 114 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 130 crore in the year-ago quarter. As a result, the company’s total income rose 25.6% to Rs 3,045 crore from Rs 2,424 crore in Q1 FY26.
Freight handling and servicing costs remained Delhivery’s largest expense, accounting for 71.45% of total expenses. The cost increased 31.4% to Rs 2,152 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,638 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Employee benefit expenses increased 21.9% to Rs 429 crore from Rs 352 crore, while depreciation rose 28.6% to Rs 189 crore from Rs 147 crore. Finance costs remained flat at Rs 34 crore, whereas other expenses climbed 33.5% to Rs 207 crore from Rs 155 crore.
The company’s total expenses rose 29.4% to Rs 3,012 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,327 crore in Q1 FY26.
Despite the strong growth in revenue, Delhivery’s profit declined 64.8% to Rs 32 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 91 crore in Q1 FY26.

On a sequential basis, Delhivery’s operating revenue increased 2.8% to Rs 2,930.73 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,850 crore in the preceding quarter, while its profit declined 55.9% to Rs 31.91 crore from Rs 72.40 crore during the same period.
Delhivery’s shares were closed at Rs 473.30 apiece on Friday, taking the company’s market capitalisation to Rs 35,198 crore.

title: Easebuzz revenue crosses Rs 700 Cr in FY26; profit plunges 42%
summary:
Full-stack payments solutions provider Easebuzz saw single-digit growth in the fiscal year ended March 2026, while its profit fell 43%. The slowdown came largely from the ban on real-money gaming apps at the start of the fiscal year, which affected the firm’s growth and profitability.

The Beesemer-backed company’s revenue from operations grew 9.1% to Rs 716 crore in FY26 from Rs 656 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Easebuzz, a B2B payment gateway for SMEs, provides plug-and-play APIs for payments, disbursements, and financial operations. In the last fiscal year, the firm generated Rs 697 crore from  transaction fees, which accounted for 97.35% of its operating revenue, while information tech and support fees contributed Rs 14 crore and SaaS fees Rs 5 crore.
Apart from operations, Easebuzz earned Rs 7 crore in other income in FY26, taking its total income to Rs 723 crore from Rs 659 crore in FY25.
For the digital payments firm, payment processing charges remained the largest cost centre, rising 2% to Rs 557 crore in FY26 from Rs 546 crore in FY25 and accounting for 78.67% of total expenses during the last fiscal year.
The $30 million funding round at the start of the fiscal year was followed by a sharp increase in Easebuzz's operating expenses. Employee benefit expenses surged 82.7% to Rs 95 crore, while information technology expenses rose 68.8% to Rs 27 crore. Advertising and promotional expenses jumped 350% to Rs 9 crore, while other expenses increased 11.1% to Rs 20 crore.
Overall, Easebuzz’s total expenses outpaced its revenue growth and rose 11.7%  year-on-year to Rs 708 crore in FY26 from Rs 634 crore in FY25.
With expenses growing faster than revenue, the company’s profitability declined in FY26. Easebuzz’s profit fell 42.1% to Rs 11 crore from Rs 19 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA declined to Rs 14 crore from Rs 28 crore, while the EBITDA margin dropped to 1.96% from 4.27%.


Its ROCE declined to 3.52% in FY26 from 18.25% in FY25. At the unit level, the company spent Rs 0.99 to earn a rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 0.97 in FY25.
As of March 2026, Easebuzz’s total current assets declined 28.4% to Rs 141 crore from Rs 197 crore in FY25, while its cash and bank balances fell 26.1% to Rs 105 crore from Rs 142 crore.

On the back of a sizable Series A round, the firm saw a sharp rise in other non-current assets, which surged over 145X to Rs 198 crore from Rs 1.37 crore in FY25, largely comprising security and long-term bank deposits.
The Pune-based firm has raised $34 million to date, including Rs 240 crore (approximately $28.2 million) in its Series A round, comprising Rs 200 crore ($23.5 million) in primary capital and Rs 40 crore ($4.7 million) in secondary capital. 8i Ventures is the largest external shareholder with a 10.88% stake, followed by Varanium Capital and Bessemer Venture Partners with 8.48% and 8.47%, respectively.
In Feb 2025, Easebuzz received final authorization from RBI to operate as an online payment aggregator and is in the process of applying for a cross-border payment aggregator license to serve international markets.
Overall, Easebuzz’s FY26 performance points to a business that struggled to convert its scale into stronger profitability. The impact of the real-money gaming ban weighed on its payment volumes, while the company continued to spend on people, technology and customer acquisition. This created pressure on margins at a time when revenue growth remained modest. With the company now expanding into regulated payment aggregation and exploring international opportunities, the key challenge will be to grow its core business while improving operating leverage and rebuilding profitability.

title: Paper Boat parent reports Rs 760 Cr revenue in FY26; profit shrinks 96%
summary:
Paper Boat maker Hector Beverages reported a steady increase in revenue during the fiscal year ended March 2026, but a sharp rise in operating expenses eroded profitability.
According to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC), the company's operating revenue increased 13.8% year-on-year to Rs 760 crore in FY26 from Rs 668 crore in FY25.

Hector Beverages sells beverages under the Paper Boat brand and competes with established players such as Dabur, PepsiCo, Coca-Cola and several regional juice and traditional beverage brands in India.
Including Rs 18 crore in other income, Hector Beverages' total income stood at Rs 778 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 682 crore in the previous fiscal year.
A shift in product mix drove the company's top line during the year. Revenue from traded goods rose 30.2% to Rs 574 crore in FY26 from Rs 441 crore in FY25 and contributed over 75% of the operating revenue. In contrast, revenue from manufactured goods declined 18.6% to Rs 184 crore from Rs 226 crore a year earlier.
The company's expenses grew at a faster pace than revenue. Total expenditure increased 22% to Rs 776 crore in FY26 from Rs 636 crore in FY25.
Consumption of materials remained the largest cost head at Rs 485 crore, accounting for 62.5% of the total expenditure, compared to Rs 447 crore in the previous year. Employee benefit expenses declined marginally to Rs 88 crore from Rs 90 crore.
The company also ramped up spending on growth and operations. Advertising and promotional expenses jumped 55.6% to Rs 28 crore, while selling and distribution expenses increased 15.5% to Rs 67 crore. Job work charges more than doubled to Rs 25 crore during the year. Other operating expenses like legal & professional, travelling expenses, rent added another Rs 83 crore in the last fiscal year.

As expenditure outpaced revenue growth, EBITDA declined 39.7% to Rs 41.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 68.6 crore in FY25. Consequently, the EBITDA margin narrowed to 5.4% from 10.3%.
The higher cost weighed heavily on the bottom line. Hector Beverages' profit after tax fell 96% to Rs 2 crore in FY26 from Rs 46 crore in the previous fiscal.
On the balance sheet, the company reported total assets of Rs 522.5 crore at the end of FY26. Its cash and bank balance declined 29% to Rs 101 crore, while current assets stood at Rs 365 crore.

title: super.money enters commerce with instalment platform splitStore
summary:
Fintech platform super.money has launched splitStore, an in app marketplace that allows users to shop across brands and pay in zero interest instalments.
The Bengaluru-based company said the feature combines shopping with embedded credit, allowing eligible users to split payments without a credit card, processing fee or interest. The offering is currently live for a select group of users, with a wider rollout underway.
According to the company, splitStore provides access to more than 60 lakh products across categories including smartphones, fashion, electronics, appliances, beauty, fitness, home and furniture. Brands available on the platform include Apple, Nothing, Nike, Adidas, Marshall, Mokobara and Snitch, while deliveries will be handled through Flipkart's logistics network.
Users can access the instalment facility after completing KYC verification, with credit offered through regulated lending partners.
"The next opportunity after UPI is transforming how India shops by making affordability a seamless part of the checkout experience," said Prakash Sikaria, founder and CEO of super.money.
With splitStore, super.money has expanded beyond UPI payments into commerce and embedded credit. The company already offers UPI payments, secured RuPay credit cards, checkout financing and personal loans through its app.
The company said splitStore has been tested with a limited group of users over the past few weeks ahead of the wider rollout.
As per data published by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), super.money was the fifth largest UPI app by transaction volume as of June, behind PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm and Navi.

title: Mobility startup E3 Electric.AI launches intelligent e-scooter E3 TRION
summary:
Bengaluru-based electric mobility startup E3 Electric.AI has launched its intelligent electric scooter, E3 TRION, which it says is designed to create a new category in the mobility space.
The AI-powered E3 TRION integrates human-centric design with predictive intelligence. Its modular architecture and smart systems are designed to continuously adapt and learn, enhancing both the riding and ownership experience over time. Complementing this is a high-efficiency powertrain engineered to balance performance and range. Together, these elements aim to address key EV ownership concerns, including range anxiety, safety, service experience, and cost.
Across its variants, the E3 TRION offers different value propositions. The C1 features a removable battery, enabling flexible and convenient charging. The C1x offers an IDC-certified range of 165 km, powered by a 3 kWh battery. The C2 variant is positioned for higher performance, with a top speed of 82 km/h and acceleration from 0 to 40 km/h in 6 seconds in Sport mode, in addition to the Eco and Power modes available in the C1 and C1x.
The E3 TRION's design combines modularity with real-world utility. From its stance and wheels to its lighting and AI layer, every element is engineered to deliver a safer, smarter, and more controlled riding experience.
Speaking about the launch, Sanjeev P., Founder and CEO of E3 Electric.AI, said, "The E3 TRION has been crafted keeping Indian families in mind, where daily commuting demands reliability, practicality, and peace of mind. By making the technology adaptive and the experience intuitive, we want everyday travel to feel smoother and more dependable. This is a meaningful step toward mobility that's not only efficient, but genuinely aligned with what modern Indian riders expect."
At the core of the E3 TRION is the E3 COMMANDCENTER, the company's proprietary E3 Intelligent IoT CORE and cloud intelligence platform. It continuously monitors each connected vehicle, predicts potential issues before they become breakdowns, enables proactive service, and delivers software improvements throughout the life of the scooter.
With more than 100 intelligent features, the system includes AI HEALTHSCAN for 10-second diagnostics, E3 Foresight predictive reports, a smart trip planner with charger locator, connected navigation and live vehicle data, remote battery monitoring and vehicle controls, a dashcam, SOS assistance, and geo-fencing.
The scooter is powered by a 2.3 kWh portable VOLTPORT battery and a 3 kWh fixed battery, both based on LFP chemistry. It is available in six colour options. The E3 TRION C1x is priced at Rs 1,09,999, while the E3 TRION C2 is priced at Rs 1,19,999.
Founded in 2024 by P. Sanjeev, E3 Electric.AI is a deep-tech electric mobility company building intelligent electric scooters with AI at their core, a modular future-ready architecture, and a human-centric design approach. The company recently raised Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) in a Series A funding round through a combination of equity and debt, led by BluVenture Holdings.

Elevation Capital, one of India's oldest venture capital firms, has realised nearly Rs 6,000 crore from partial stake sales in listed Indian technology companies over the past 15 months through IPO offer for sale transactions, block deals and bulk deals, while continuing to hold listed startup investments worth more than Rs 20,000 crore (over $2 billion) across Meesho, Paytm and Urban Company.
The latest stake sale came on Tuesday, when Elevation Capital sold shares worth Rs 974.5 crore in Meesho through a block deal by offloading 1.49 crore shares. The transaction followed another major stake sale earlier this week, when Elevation Capital, through its investment entities, sold a 2.33% stake in Paytm in a block deal worth Rs 2,038 crore by offloading 1.49 crore shares at Rs 1,367.8 apiece.
These transactions are part of a series of partial stake sales over the past 15 months. In November 2025, Elevation sold shares worth Rs 1,556 crore in Paytm. It also pared its holding in ixigo through four transactions between May and October 2025, realising around Rs 808 crore. Apart from secondary market stake sales, the firm also monetised part of its investments through IPO offer for sale transactions, selling shares worth Rs 271 crore in Meesho's public issue and Rs 346 crore in Urban Company's IPO.

Overall, Elevation Capital has realised nearly Rs 5,993 crore through partial stake sales in Indian technology companies over the past 15 months via IPO offer for sale transactions, block deals and bulk deals. The transactions illustrate how venture capital firms monetise mature investments during IPOs and through secondary market transactions after listing.
Despite these partial stake sales, the firm continues to hold sizeable stakes in several listed startups. Following the latest block deal, Elevation's remaining stake in Meesho is valued at around Rs 9,550 crore (over $1 billion) at the prevailing market price. It also holds a stake worth around Rs 9,015 crore (about $950 million) in Paytm through SAIF III Mauritius and SAIF Partners India IV, while its holding in Urban Company is valued at approximately Rs 1,793 crore (about $189 million). The remaining stake values are based on prevailing market prices following Tuesday's block deal.
Queries sent to Elevation Capital on Wednesday did not receive a response until the publication of this story.
The sizeable residual portfolio underscores that despite selective stake sales, Elevation Capital remains among the largest institutional shareholders in several listed new-age technology companies.

title: D2C athleisure brand BlissClub raises Rs 160 Cr in Series B led by Singularity AMC
summary:
D2C athleisure brand BlissClub has raised Rs 160 crore ($16.8 million) in a Series B funding round led by Singularity AMC. Founder Minu Margeret and her partner Vidit Aatrey also participated in the round, alongside existing investors Elevation Capital and Eight Roads Ventures.
The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised $15 million in its Series A round in May 2022, led by Eight Roads Ventures with participation from Elevation Capital.
According to the company, the fresh capital will be used to expand into new categories, scale its offline retail presence, strengthen product development, and hire talent to support its next phase of growth.
Founded in 2020 by Minu Margeret, BlissClub is a direct-to-consumer (D2C) athleisure and functional apparel brand. The company initially focused on technical activewear for Indian women and has since expanded into an omnichannel business with more than 40 retail stores and a recently launched menswear line.
Its portfolio includes leggings, tops, outerwear, and accessories developed through in-house research and sourcing. The brand sells through its own website, marketplaces, and offline retail stores across India.
BlissClub has yet to file its annual financial report for FY26. In FY25, its operating revenue grew 51% to Rs 131.5 crore in FY25 from Rs 87 crore in FY24. During the same period, the company also reduced its losses by more than half, aided by lower employee costs.

title: Exclusive: PayGlocal set to raise fresh funding at $120 Mn valuation
summary:
Cross-border payments startup PayGlocal is set to raise Rs 36.38 crore ($3.84 million) from existing investor BEENEXTin its first funding round in more than four years.
PayGlocal last raised $12 million in its Series B round led by Tiger Global, with participation from Sequoia Capital India and BEENEXT. Entrackr had exclusively reported the round.
The board at PayGlocal has passed a special resolution to issue 5,074 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 71,693.02 per share to raise Rs 36.38 crore, according to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, the Bengaluru based company's valuation will increase 31.8% to Rs 1,140 crore or ($120 million) from Rs 865 crore in its previous funding round.
Founded in 2021 by Prachi Dharani, Rohit Sukhija, and Yogesh Lokhande, PayGlocal provides RBI-authorised cross-border payment infrastructure that enables Indian businesses to accept international payments. The company earns revenue by offering payment gateway, multi-currency collection, export documentation, fraud prevention, and settlement solutions to exporters, SaaS firms, D2C brands, marketplaces, and freelancers.
Following the allotment, Peak XV will remain the largest external shareholder with a 34.04% stake, followed by BeeNext (6.14%) and Tiger Global (5.21%), while co-founders Prachi Dharani, Rohit Sukhija, and Yogesh Lokhande will hold 18.92%, 14.19%, and 13.37%, respectively.
Prior to this round the company has raised around $17 million to date. Key investors Tiger Global, Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV Partners), BEENEXT, and other existing investors. 

The company is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. In FY25, PayGlocal's operating revenue more than doubled to Rs 25.11 crore from Rs 12.20 crore in FY24, while its losses declined to Rs 14 crore from Rs 15.31 crore.

title: Exclusive: Dosa chain Benne raises Rs 35 Cr led by Rajan pai's Claypond Capital
summary:
Mumbai-based dosa chain Benne has raised Rs 35 crore (around $3.70 million) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Ranjan pAi’ Claypond Capital.
The company's board has passed a resolution to issue 1,799 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 20,349 each to raise the aforementioned amount, according to its regulatory filing accessed by Entrackr.
The round was led by Ranjan Pai's family office, Claypond Capital, which invested Rs 28.75 crore. AL Trusts invested Rs 3.5 crore, followed by Mukul Agrawal with Rs 1.75 crore. Madhukeshwar Desai and Cortado Advisory Services also participated, investing Rs 75 lakh and Rs 25 lakh, respectively.
According to Entrackr's estimates, the round valued the company at around Rs 364 crore (approximately $38.3 million) on a post-money basis. The fresh proceeds will be deployed towards expanding the company's operations and supporting its growth plans.
In April, Moneycontrol reported that Benne was in talks to raise Rs 35–40 crore in a funding round led by Claypond Capital.
Founded by husband-wife duo Akhil Iyer and Shriya Narayan, Benne is a quick service restaurant (QSR) chain focused on authentic Bengaluru-style dosas. The brand generates revenue through dine-in, takeaway, and food delivery, with a limited menu and compact outlets driving operational efficiency and consistent quality.
Following the allotment of this round, Claypond Capital Partners became the largest external investor with an 8.21% stake, followed by Mukul Mahavir Agrawal (5%), Madhukeshwar Desai (3.85%), AL Trust (1%), and Cortado Advisory Services (0.07%).

Benne competes with The Rameshwaram Cafe, Cafe Amudham, and other premium South Indian QSR brands.

title: Ixigo posts Rs 357 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit rises 81%
summary:
Online travel aggregator (OTA) Ixigo released its financial results for the first quarter of the ongoing fiscal year ending March 2027 on Thursday. The company reported an 13% year-on-year growth in revenue, while its profit rose 81% to Rs 34 crore during the same period.
Ixigo’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 356.75 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 316.05 crore in Q1 FY26, according to the company’s unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).


 
The Gurugram-based company derived the largest share of its operating revenue from train ticketing, which contributed more than 39% of the total in the quarter. Revenue from the segment rose to Rs 141.05 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 129.92 crore in the year ago period. Flight and bus ticketing generated Rs 104.56 crore and Rs 102.55 crore, respectively.
Apart from operating revenue, the company reported Rs 29.15 crore from interest income and gains on financial assets, pushing its total income to Rs 385.9 crore in Q1 FY27.
According to its press release, Ixigo's gross transaction value (GTV) increased 19% year on year to Rs 5,524.33 crore during the quarter.
The company did not disclose a detailed expense breakup in its quarterly financial statements. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 58.59 crore, while total expenses rose 14.7% to Rs 337.76 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 294.35 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Ixigo's profit rose 81% to Rs 34.34 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 18.94 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. On a sequential basis, profit increased 6.8% from Rs 32 crore in Q4 FY26.
Its listed peer MakeMyTrip reported revenue of $286 million in Q1 FY27, while profit declined 65% to $9.2 million during the same period.
Ixigo's shares closed at Rs 202.67 on Thursday, valuing the online travel aggregator at a market capitalization of Rs 8,775 crore.

title: Shiprocket crosses Rs 2,000 Cr revenue in FY26; loss rises 7% to Rs 79 Cr
summary:
Logistics and e-commerce enablement platform Shiprocket crossed the Rs 2,000 crore revenue mark in FY26, with operating revenue rising 24% year-on-year, while its losses widened 7% to Rs 79 crore ahead of its public listing.

Zomato-backed Shiprocket reported a 24% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 2,024 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,632 crore in the previous fiscal, according to its financial statements disclosed in the RHP.

While Shiprocket's core business, comprising its domestic shipping platform and value-added technology offerings, grew 13.7% year-on-year to Rs 1,485 crore, contributing 73.4% of total operating revenue, its emerging businesses, including the cross-border platform, marketing, and omnichannel offerings, generated the remaining Rs 539 crore, up 65% year-on-year.
The firm also earned Rs 53 crore from non-operating sources such as interest on fixed deposits, which took its total income to Rs 2,077 crore during the year.
Shiprocket's largest cost, materials consumed, increased 24.1% year-on-year to Rs 1,515 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 380 crore, including Rs 112 crore towards ESOPs.
Server and communication costs stood at Rs 58 crore, while advertising and promotional expenses jumped 71% year-on-year to Rs 36 crore. Higher spending across warehouse management, depreciation and amortisation, finance costs, and other overheads pushed the company's total expenditure up 23% to Rs 2,153 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,749 crore in the previous fiscal.
With revenue and expenses growing at a similar pace, Shiprocket's net loss increased marginally by 7% to Rs 79 crore in FY26 from Rs 74 crore a year earlier. The loss included Rs 112 crore in ESOP expenses.
The company spent Rs 1.06 to earn every rupee of operating revenue compared with Rs 1.07 in the previous fiscal. Its EBITDA margin and ROCE -3.31% ROCE stood at -6.39% in FY26.

As of March 2026, It reported current assets of Rs 1,017 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 188 crore. 
Shiprocket has trimmed its IPO size by 31% to Rs 1,617.48 crore from Rs 2,342.35 crore proposed in the UDRHP. The reduction includes a cut in the fresh issue to Rs 885.5 crore from Rs 1,100 crore and the OFS to Rs 731.98 crore from Rs 1,242.35 crore.

summary:
Chennai based deeptech startup Solinas Integrity has raised $5.5 million in a Series A1 funding round co led by Mela Ventures and Hero Enterprise Family Office.
The round also saw participation from Luthra Group along with follow on investments from existing backers SVL SME Fund, managed by SBI Ventures, Rainmatter Capital, and 8X Ventures Fund I.
The fresh capital will be deployed to expand manufacturing capacity, accelerate product development, strengthen the company's software infrastructure, and support working capital requirements. Solinas also plans to expand its presence in international markets, particularly the Middle East and Southeast Asia, while developing new robotics solutions for the water, sanitation, industrial, and defence sectors.
Founded in 2018 by Divanshu Kumar and Moinak Banerjee, the IIT Madras incubated startup builds robotics and AI powered solutions for underground water and sanitation infrastructure. Its product portfolio includes Endobot for pipeline inspection, HomoSEP for mechanised sewer and septic tank cleaning, and SWASTH AI, an infrastructure intelligence platform that uses inspection data for asset mapping and predictive analytics.
According to the company, its solutions have been deployed across more than 30 cities in 15 Indian states and are also in use by Dubai Municipality.
The company said it is also expanding into adjacent sectors such as oil and gas and defence, where its robotics and inspection technologies can be applied to critical infrastructure.
Solinas operates in the water, sanitation and hygiene segment, where utilities increasingly rely on mechanised inspection and maintenance tools to reduce water losses and improve underground infrastructure management. The startup says its integrated robotics platform enables inspection, cleaning, digitisation, and lifecycle management of underground water and wastewater networks.

summary:
Nazara Technologies has approved a preferential issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 733.5 crore. The proposal awaits shareholder and regulatory approvals.
The board approved the issuance of up to 2,39,70,676 equity shares at an issue price of Rs 306 apiece, including a premium of Rs 304 per share, to six identified investors on a preferential basis.
The proposed allottees are Raymond Albaladejo Stauffer, Marc Sylvester Schutze, Maxime Loppin, Alexandre Paul Jean Noirot Cosson, Alexander Osou and Hugo Rémy Gaston Blavin.
Stauffer, who was appointed Nazara's chief executive officer earlier this week and will assume the role from September 1, is set to receive the largest allotment of 1,90,67,969 shares. Following the allotment, he will hold a 4.67% stake in the company.
The remaining investors will receive 28,32,273 shares, 10,03,628 shares, 7,10,946 shares, 2,66,895 shares and 88,965 shares, respectively. Collectively, the six investors will own a 5.87% stake in Nazara after the preferential issue.
The fundraising comes three days after Nazara reported a weak start to FY27. The company posted a 14% year on year decline in operating revenue to Rs 429 crore in the June quarter from Rs 499 crore in the year ago period. It also slipped to a net loss of Rs 82 crore against a net profit of Rs 51 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal. The loss included Rs 62 crore as its share of losses from associates and a Rs 22 crore impairment charge.
The board also announced a leadership transition earlier this week. Founder Nitish Mittersain stepped down as chief executive officer and will continue as managing director, focusing on the company's long term strategy and strategic partnerships, while Stauffer will take over as CEO from September 1.

title: Shiprocket IPO: Early investors set for up to 78X returns, late-stage backers face losses
summary:
The public listing of logistics unicorn Shiprocket is set to reward several of its early investors with multi-fold returns, while some late-stage backers are expected to incur losses on their partial exits. 
According to the company's Red Herring Prospectus (RHP), Shiprocket has reduced its IPO size by 31% to Rs 1,617.48 crore from Rs 2,342.35 crore proposed in the updated DRHP. The fresh issue has been cut to Rs 885.5 crore from Rs 1,100 crore, while the offer for sale (OFS) has been reduced to Rs 731.98 crore from Rs 1,242.35 crore.
According to Entrackr's analysis, at the upper price band of Rs 97 per share, early investor 500 Global is set to emerge as the biggest winner, generating an estimated 77.6X return on its Rs 16 crore OFS. Tribe Capital is expected to earn around 7.7X on its Rs 120 crore OFS, while Agility International Investment and March Capital are likely to generate returns of 2.6X and 2.1X on their Rs 21 crore and Rs 56 crore OFS, respectively.

However, the picture is marked differently for investors who entered Shiprocket at higher valuations in later funding rounds. Lightrock, the largest selling shareholder with an OFS worth Rs 272 crore, is expected to earn only 0.72X on the shares being sold. McKinsey through AFOS and Moore Strategic Partners are also likely to exit with returns of 0.59X and 0.67X, respectively, indicating that they are selling below their acquisition cost.
Founder shareholders Saahil Goel, Gautam Kapoor and Vishesh Khurana will also partially pare their holdings through the OFS. Gautam Kapoor and Saahil Goel are each selling shares worth Rs 61 crore, while Vishesh Khurana will offload shares worth Rs 20 crore.
Notably, Shiprocket's largest shareholder, Bertelsmann India Investments, which was included in the OFS in the earlier UDRHP, has opted out of the final offer. Major shareholders Eternal (formerly Zomato) and Temasek will also not participate in the OFS.
The IPO will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14, with the anchor book opening on August 11.

title: Leap India raises Rs 371 Cr in pre-IPO round led by GIC arm
summary:
KKR-backed supply chain solutions firm Leap India has raised Rs 371.3 crore in a pre-IPO placement from Singapore-based sovereign wealth fund GIC's subsidiary Gamnat Pte Ltd, hedge fund Dymon Asia Multi-Strategy Investment (Singapore), and promoter Sunu Mathew, a day before its public issue opens. 
According to a public advertisement published by the company, Leap India allotted 2.33 crore equity shares at Rs 159 apiece. Gamnat Pte Ltd emerged as the largest investor in the round, investing Rs 280 crore for 1.76 crore shares. Dymon Asia Multi-Strategy Investment invested Rs 50 crore, while Matyas Possessiones Private Limited, in which promoter Sunu Mathew owns a 99% stake, infused Rs 23 crore. 
Leap India had filed its red herring prospectus (RHP) last week for a Rs 2,480 crore initial public offering, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 480 crore and an offer for sale of Rs 2,000 crore by existing shareholders. The issue is scheduled to open on August 7 and close on August 11.
The fresh capital will be used to repay borrowings, fund capital expenditure for the purchase of pallets, crates and intermediate bulk containers, and for general corporate purposes.

Co-founded in 2023 by Devdut Dalal and Xavier Laguarta Soler, Mitti Labs uses satellite imagery and AI to support water efficient farming practices. The company generates carbon credits by verifying emission reductions from these practices and sells them to corporations pursuing net zero emission goals.
Headquartered in Bengaluru and New York, Mitti Labs operates in the AgTech, climate smart agriculture, digital Measurement, Reporting and Verification (dMRV), and carbon credits segments. According to the company, it works with tens of thousands of farmers across multiple Indian states, covering more than 70,000 hectares.
Mitti Labs says its technology can reduce water usage by up to 40% and methane emissions by around 50%. It combines synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite imagery with ground level field measurements to build digital twins of individual rice plots for monitoring and carbon accounting. The company also said its projects in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh received an 'A' rating from carbon credit ratings agency Sylvera.

title: Shiprocket trims IPO size by 31% in RHP to Rs 1,617 Cr; issue to open on August 12
summary:
Logistics and e-commerce enablement platform Shiprocket has reduced the size of its initial public offering (IPO) by 31% in its red herring prospectus (RHP), lowering the fresh issue to Rs 1,617.48 crore from earlier proposed Rs 2,342.35 crore in UDRHP.
The IPO will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14, with the anchor book opening on August 11. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 92 to Rs 97 per share. At the upper price band, the company will be valued at around Rs 7,057 crore or $743 million.
According to the RHP, the company has reduced the fresh issue size to Rs 885.5 crore from the Rs 1,100 crore proposed earlier. The offer also includes an offer for sale (OFS) worth Rs 731.98 crore by existing shareholders, down from the previously proposed size.
The OFS will be led by Lightrock, which plans to sell shares worth Rs 271.7 crore, followed by Tribe Capital and March Capital (through MCP3 SPV LLC), which will offload shares worth Rs 120 crore and Rs 55.53 crore, respectively. Other selling shareholders include 500 Startups, Agility Global, and Moore Strategic Ventures.
The company's co-founders Gautam Kapoor and Saahil Goel have reduced their OFS to Rs 61 crore each, while Vishesh Khurana will sell shares worth Rs 20 crore.
Notably, Arvid Ltd and Bertelsmann India Investments, which were part of the OFS in the earlier UDRHP, have opted not to participate in the RHP.
The company plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue primarily to expand its platform across both its core and emerging businesses. Of the total, Rs 365.6 crore has been earmarked for growth initiatives, including Rs 205.8 crore for marketing and Rs 159.8 crore for technology infrastructure and capabilities. Another Rs 210 crore will be used to repay borrowings, while the remaining proceeds will support inorganic growth through acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
The IPO is being managed by Axis Capital, BofA Securities, JM Financial and Kotak, while KFin Technologies will act as registrar.
As per the RHP, Bertelsmann India Investments remains the company's largest shareholder with a 21.32% stake, followed by Tribe Capital with 14.14%. Eternal (formerly Zomato) holds 6.85%, while Temasek owns 5.29%. Co-founders Saahil Goel and Gautam Kapoor each hold a 4.84% stake, and the ESOP pool represents 5.97% of the company's shareholding.
Financially, the Gurugram-based company reported a 24% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 2,024 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,632 crore in FY25. Its net loss also increased 6.8% to Rs 79 crore during the same period.

title: Policybazaar parent PB Fintech's profit jumps 92% to Rs 163 crore in Q1 FY27
summary:
PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar announced its Q1 FY27 results today. The company reported a 92% year-on-year jump in profit after tax to Rs 163 crore.
The Gurugram-based company posted operating revenue of Rs 1,888 crore in Q1 FY27, a 40% increase from Rs 1,348 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, as per the firm’s financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Revenue from the core online business was led by Policybazaar, which contributed Rs 1,067 crore, while Paisabazaar added Rs 127 crore. The company's new initiatives, including PB Partners, PB for Business, PB UAE and PB Connect, collectively generated Rs 694 crore.
In addition to operating revenue, the firm earned Rs 93 crore from interest and gains on financial assets during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 1,981 crore for the quarter ended March 2026.
On a quarterly basis, PB Fintech’s revenue dropped over 8% from Rs 2,061 crore in Q4 FY26.
The company's total insurance premium rose 41% year-on-year to Rs 8,372 crore during the quarter, led by a 53% increase in new protection premium, including a 59% growth in health insurance premium. 
Employee benefit expenses remained the group's largest cost, accounting for 40% of total expenditure at Rs 716 crore, a 28% increase from the year-ago quarter. Advertising and promotional expenses also climbed 50% year-on-year to Rs 379 crore in Q1 FY27.
The company did not provide a detailed breakup of other expenses in its quarterly financials. Overall expenditure rose 33% year-on-year to Rs 1,800 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,356 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Coming to the bottom line, the group's profit after tax surged 92% year-on-year to Rs 163 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 85 crore in the same quarter last year, led by a 41% year-on-year growth in insurance premium.
However, on a sequential basis, PB Fintech's profit declined more than 37% from Rs 261 crore in Q4 FY26.
At the end of today’s trading session, shares of PB Fintech closed at Rs 1,620, taking its total market capitalization to Rs 74,957 crore (about $7.89 billion).

title: River Mobility raises $120 Mn in Series C led by Elev8, Claypond Capital
summary:
Electric two wheeler maker River Mobility has raised $120 million in a Series C funding round comprising equity and venture debt, one of the largest private funding rounds in India's electric two wheeler segment.
The equity round was led by Elev8 Venture Partners and Claypond Capital, with participation from Singularity AMC, Anicut Capital, 360 ONE Asset, JIF Capital and HDFC AMC. Existing investors including Yamaha Motor Corporation, Al Futtaim Group and Mitsui & Co also participated, while Alteria Capital, Innoven Capital and Stride Ventures joined through venture debt.
Founded in 2021 by Aravind Mani and Vipin George, River Mobility manufactures electric two wheelers with a focus on utility oriented products. Its flagship electric scooter, Indie, was launched in 2023.
The company will use the fresh capital to expand capacity at its existing manufacturing facility, set up a new greenfield plant, launch new products in the utility lifestyle segment, and improve gross margins and EBITDA profitability.
"This funding marks an important milestone in River's journey. The confidence shown by both our existing and new investors reinforces our belief that there is tremendous opportunity to build India's first utility and design based mobility brand," said Aravind Mani, co-founder and CEO of River Mobility.
River currently operates more than 75 retail stores across India and plans to expand its network to over 350 stores by March 2028.
According to the company, monthly sales have reached around 5,000 units over the past year as it continues to expand its manufacturing capacity and distribution network. It also plans to introduce new electric vehicle models over the coming years.
In February 2024, River raised $40 million in a Series B funding round led by Yamaha, with participation from Al Futtaim Group, Lowercarbon Capital, Toyota Ventures and Maniv Mobility. Prior to that, it had secured $15 million in a Series A round in June 2023.
With the latest financing, River has raised around $188 million across equity and venture debt since its inception. The latest round also marks the company's first major backing from Indian institutional investors, adding to its existing global investor base that includes Yamaha Motor Corporation, Marubeni Corporation, Mitsui & Co, Al Futtaim Group, Lowercarbon Capital, Toyota Ventures, Maniv Mobility and Trucks VC.

title: Swiggy outlines exclusive product strategy for Instamart, sees cash break-even in two quarters
summary:
While Swiggy's quarterly results highlighted continued investments in quick commerce, the company's earnings call offered fresh insight into how it plans to differentiate Instamart in an increasingly competitive market. Rather than focusing only on network expansion, management outlined a strategy centred on exclusive products, private labels and brand partnerships, while reiterating its path towards cash break-even over the next two quarters.
A key announcement during the call was the launch of "Switch to Better", an initiative aimed at offering differentiated products on Instamart. According to management, the programme brings together large FMCG companies, challenger brands and Swiggy's own private labels to develop products that are available only on the platform.
The company said exclusivity often extends to individual SKUs rather than entire brands. For example, multiple high-protein oat variants have been developed exclusively for Instamart, while some brands offer exclusive pricing on the platform. In categories such as eggs, Swiggy is promoting its own private label. Management said the objective is to provide customers with better products at competitive prices.
Executives also indicated that the strategy is category-specific. Depending on the segment, Instamart works with established FMCG brands, emerging direct-to-consumer companies or its own private labels. The company believes this approach can help build differentiation as competition in quick commerce intensifies.
Beyond merchandising, Swiggy shared an update on profitability. Chief Financial Officer Rahul Bothra said improving margins in the food delivery business and treasury income are expected to help the company achieve overall cash break-even within the next two quarters, even as investments in quick commerce continue.
Management also outlined its capital allocation framework for new businesses. It said emerging initiatives are first evaluated for product-market fit and business-market fit before receiving additional investment. Once those milestones are achieved, businesses are expected to scale with clear unit economics rather than relying on continued capital deployment.
The company added that it will share more details on its broader strategy during its upcoming Investor Day.
The earnings call suggests Swiggy is gradually moving beyond competing only on delivery speed. While rapid fulfillment remains the foundation of Instamart, the company's next phase appears to hinge on offering products that customers cannot easily find elsewhere. Through exclusive SKUs, private labels and brand partnerships, Swiggy is attempting to build a differentiated shopping experience that can improve customer retention and margins as competition in quick commerce intensifies.

title: Tracxn slips into loss as revenue remains flat in Q1 FY27
summary:
Data intelligence platform Tracxn announced its Q1 FY27 results on Wednesday. The Bengaluru-based company reported flat revenue during the quarter, while it slipped into losses.

Tracxn’s revenue from operations declined 0.6% to Rs 21.08 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 21.20 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal (Q1 FY26), according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Tracxn derived its entire operating revenue from subscription sales that provide access to its data and software. However, the company did not disclose a detailed revenue breakup for the quarter.
The company also earned Rs 1.52 crore from non operating sources, taking its total revenue to Rs 22.60 crore in the first quarter of FY27.
Employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost head, increasing 16% to Rs 21.98 crore and accounting for 86.64% of the overall expenditure during the quarter. The company’s total expenses rose 18.4% to Rs 25.37 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 21.43 crore in Q1 FY26.
Due to the sharp increase in expenses, Tracxn reported a loss of Rs 3.01 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to a profit of Rs 1.12 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On a quarter on quarter basis, Tracxn reported a marginal 2.9% growth in operating revenue to Rs 21.08 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 20.49 crore in Q4 FY26. However, its losses widened 14.4% to Rs 3.01 crore during the same period from Rs 2.63 crore in the preceding quarter.
At the close of trading on Monday, Tracxn's shares settled at Rs 30.62, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately Rs 319 crore.
